findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` instead of `||`; since `isTeamOwner` implies `isTeamAdmin`, the expression reduces to "is owner only", so team ADMINs are incorrectly denied from adding guests to team bookings (contradicts the variable name and intent)

[Medium/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158-165 — `EventManager` is built with the requesting user's credentials (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`), but `updateCalendarAttendees` matches `booking.references[].credentialId` against those credentials; when an attendee or team admin (not the organizer) triggers the mutation, no credential matches and the calendar event is silently never updated — even though the organizer's credentials were already fetched via `booking.user.include.credentials` (lines 35-38) and left unused

[Medium/security] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70-77 — blacklist check is case-sensitive on the guest side: blacklist entries are lowercased but `guest` is not, so "User@Spam.com" bypasses a "user@spam.com" `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` entry; emails should be trimmed/lowercased before the check and before storage (same normalization gap affects the attendee dedup at line 76 and `isAttendee` at line 52)

[Medium/data] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:3-6 — server schema enforces neither uniqueness nor a max count on `guests`; uniqueness exists only in the client component (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29); a direct API call with `["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` passes the handler's filter (which only dedupes against existing attendees, not within the array) and `createMany` inserts duplicate attendee rows, producing duplicate emails/ICS sends

[Medium/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44-56 — no check of `booking.status` (or whether the booking is in the past); guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, sending "Guests Added" notifications with `method: "REQUEST"` / `status: "CONFIRMED"` iCal payloads that can resurrect a cancelled meeting on attendees' calendars

[Medium/data] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92-106 — for event types with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, there is no capacity validation and `createMany` bypasses the seat/`BookingSeat` logic entirely, so attendees can be added beyond the seat limit of a seated booking

[Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the raw input instead of `uniqueGuests`; an existing attendee whose email is re-entered (filtered out of the DB write) still matches `newGuests.includes(...)` in email-manager.ts and receives a duplicate full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the "guests added" notification

[Low/bug] apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33 — `isInvalidEmail` is only reset by the Cancel button; it persists when the dialog is closed via overlay/Escape or after a successful submit, so the "Emails must be unique and valid" banner is displayed immediately on reopen with a fresh form

[Low/concurrency] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26-42,92-106 — the duplicate check (read attendees) and the insert (`booking.update` + `createMany`) are separate non-transactional operations; two concurrent requests adding the same guest both pass the check and create duplicate attendee records

[Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — email-send failures are swallowed with `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` (error object not logged, `console.log` instead of the logger) and the mutation still returns success, so users see "Guests added" even when notifications failed

[Low/security] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — `guests` array has no `.max()` bound; a single authenticated request can trigger an unbounded number of outbound emails and calendar API calls (email-bombing/abuse vector)

[Low/bug] packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:25 — list items use `key={index}` while rows can be removed from the middle; React reuses the same DOM inputs for shifted values on removal, which can cause stale/focused input state when deleting an email

[Low/test_gap] no tests accompany the new mutation: the authorization matrix (organizer/attendee/team admin/team owner), dedup/blacklist filtering, seated-event capacity, and the `sendAddGuestsEmails` template-selection logic (new vs. existing attendees) are all untested

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158-165 — `EventManager` is built with the requesting user's credentials (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`), but `updateCalendarAttendees` matches `booking.references[].credentialId` against those credentials; when an attendee or team admin (not the organizer) triggers the mutation, no credential matches and the calendar event is silently never updated — even though the organizer's credentials were already fetched via `booking.user.include.credentials` (lines 35-38) and left unused

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers to run it (`isAttendee` check and `isTeamAdminOrOwner` path), but it builds `EventManager` using `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (the requesting user) and then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. The booking query already includes the organizer user’s `credentials` (`booking.user.include.credentials`) but those are never used. Given the intent to update the booking’s calendar event (which is typically tied to the organizer/booking owner credentials), using the requester’s credentials will likely prevent updating the organizer’s calendar when the requester is an attendee/admin, causing the calendar not to be updated even though attendees were added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44-56 — no check of `booking.status` (or whether the booking is in the past); guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, sending "Guests Added" notifications with `method: "REQUEST"` / `status: "CONFIRMED"` iCal payloads that can resurrect a cancelled meeting on attendees' calendars

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuestsHandler`, the booking is fetched and updated (attendees `createMany`) with no validation of booking lifecycle (no check for a cancelled/rejected status or for `startTime` being in the past). The subsequent notification path always generates ICS payloads with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` in both `packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, and `sendAddGuestsEmails` is invoked unconditionally after updating. This can lead to sending “Guests Added” calendar updates that appear as confirmed meeting requests even for bookings that should no longer be active.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92-106 — for event types with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, there is no capacity validation and `createMany` bypasses the seat/`BookingSeat` logic entirely, so attendees can be added beyond the seat limit of a seated booking

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, new guests are appended via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` with no checks against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (even though it’s read into `evt.seatsPerTimeSlot`). The diff shows no capacity validation and no alternative seat-specific persistence (e.g., creating seat records) before adding attendees, so for seated events this can exceed the intended seat limit and bypass any seat/`BookingSeat` enforcement that would normally constrain attendee count.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33 — `isInvalidEmail` is only reset by the Cancel button; it persists when the dialog is closed via overlay/Escape or after a successful submit, so the "Emails must be unique and valid" banner is displayed immediately on reopen with a fresh form

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on validation failure in `handleAdd`, but it is only reset to `false` in the Cancel button onClick handler. The dialog can also be closed via `Dialog`'s `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` (overlay click / Escape), which does not reset `isInvalidEmail`. Additionally, `onSuccess` closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue` but does not reset `isInvalidEmail`, so the error banner (`{isInvalidEmail && ...}`) can persist and show immediately when the dialog is reopened.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/concurrency] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26-42,92-106 — the duplicate check (read attendees) and the insert (`booking.update` + `createMany`) are separate non-transactional operations; two concurrent requests adding the same guest both pass the check and create duplicate attendee records

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler reads the booking + existing attendees (`prisma.booking.findFirst(... include: { attendees: true })`), computes `uniqueGuests` from that snapshot, then later performs a separate `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` without a transaction or other atomic guard. The diff does show a classic TOCTOU window where concurrent requests can both decide the same email is “unique” and race to insert. Whether this results in duplicated rows vs a DB constraint error isn’t verifiable from the diff (no attendee unique index shown), but the non-atomic pattern is real and can cause duplicate inserts or failed requests under concurrency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — email-send failures are swallowed with `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` (error object not logged, `console.log` instead of the logger) and the mutation still returns success, so users see "Guests added" even when notifications failed

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the email notification send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") }` and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This does swallow the error (doesn’t log `err` and uses `console.log`), but the primary mutation work (DB attendee creation + `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`) has already succeeded, so returning success is not necessarily incorrect—this is mainly an observability/UX concern rather than a definite functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/security] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — `guests` array has no `.max()` bound; a single authenticated request can trigger an unbounded number of outbound emails and calendar API calls (email-bombing/abuse vector)

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the request directly drives work proportional to the number of emails: it creates many attendee rows (`createMany`), updates calendar attendees with the full attendee list (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`), and sends emails for every attendee via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which maps over `calendarEvent.attendees` to enqueue outbound emails. With no `.max()` (or other rate/size guard) in the schema or handler, a single authenticated call can trigger a very large amount of outbound email/calendar operations, matching the abuse vector described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:25 — list items use `key={index}` while rows can be removed from the middle; React reuses the same DOM inputs for shifted values on removal, which can cause stale/focused input state when deleting an email

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the email inputs are rendered with `value.map((field, index) => ( <li key={index}> ... ))` while an email can be removed from the middle via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. Using the array index as the React key in a mutable list can cause React to reuse DOM nodes for subsequent rows after deletion, leading to mismatched input state (e.g., stale value/cursor/focus moving to the wrong row). This is a real behavior risk directly shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] no tests accompany the new mutation: the authorization matrix (organizer/attendee/team admin/team owner), dedup/blacklist filtering, seated-event capacity, and the `sendAddGuestsEmails` template-selection logic (new vs. existing attendees) are all untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior (new `viewer.bookings.addGuests` mutation wired in `_router.tsx`, implemented in `addGuests.handler.ts`, plus `sendAddGuestsEmails` in `email-manager.ts` with new templates). There are no accompanying test changes in the diff, and the new logic includes nontrivial branches worth covering: role/permission gating (`isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner`, organizer, attendee), guest filtering against existing attendees + `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`, and email-template selection in `sendAddGuestsEmails` (choosing between `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` based on whether an attendee is in `newGuests`). The finding’s mention of seated-event capacity is not grounded in this diff (no capacity/seats checks were added here), but the core “new mutation logic is untested” concern is specific and diff-backed.
